$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
base: ff06655f (tejas/win-267-compose, the head of PR #153, still OPEN against v1)
purpose: G2 gives `governance`'s three inverted READ SEAMS their first implementation,
as three rows on `packages/adapters/postgres-tenancy` — the directory that is
already the canonical store of all four tables they read.
THE ENTRIES THIS LEDGER EXISTS FOR ARE M01, M02, M10, M11 AND M12. Every one
of them removes a TENANT NARROWING, and every one of them leaves a reader
that type-checks, answers plausible values, and serves another tenant's rows.
`Turn` has no `environmentId` column at all, so its tenancy is a JOIN and the
type system has nothing to say about losing it. They are killed against a
REAL PostgreSQL with TWO tenants seeded, because a double cannot have this
bug: `InMemoryRatingTargets` stores an `environmentId` beside every seeded
turn precisely because it has nowhere else to put one.
M08 SURVIVED ON THE FIRST RUN AND IS RECORDED WITH THE CASE THAT NOW KILLS
IT. Deleting the PROJECT limb of `narrowableScope`'s uuid check left all 27
cases green: the suite blanked the ENVIRONMENT and never the other two. An
unguarded limb is not a smaller guard — the value reaches a `@db.Uuid`
column, the driver raises, and `refuse()` reports it as
GOVERNANCE_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE, which is the one shared code these three
constructors exist to stay out of. A nineteenth case blanks the project and
the organization across all three seams; M08 and M16 both kill against it.
M17, M18 AND M19 MUTATE THINGS THIS BRANCH DOES NOT CONTROL — `schema.prisma`,
the initial migration, and the shipped `docs/error-taxonomy.json` — and watch
`governance-read-seams.test.ts` go red. Without them, that suite's claims
('`Turn` has no environment of its own', '`Turn_ancestry` ties the version to
the thread's agent', 'all three codes are internal/500') would be assertions
about strings this tranche wrote.
WHAT IS NOT A MUTATION AND IS RECORDED AS A DIVERGENCE INSTEAD: the two
defects the ORACLE found. `apps/agent/src/evals/rating.service.ts` and
`apps/agent/src/monitoring/governance.service.ts` are byte-identical to
origin/main and implement all three of these questions. Reading them found
the readers wrong twice — an environment-only tenant filter where the oracle
uses the whole triple, and `toolErrors` counting FAILED where the oracle
counts FAILED or CANCELLED. Neither was reachable by mutation, because every
assertion on this branch compared the readers to themselves. See `oracle`.
procedure: Every mutation is applied to ONE file, built, and run INDIVIDUALLY. The
container suite runs on the Mac mini over ssh (Docker is quit on the laptop
by standing instruction) against pgvector/pgvector:pg16 through
@testcontainers/postgresql; M17-M19 need no container and ran on the laptop.
A CONTEXT EDIT DOES NOT REACH AN ADAPTER SUITE UNTIL THE CONTEXT'S dist/ IS
RE-EMITTED — WIN-267 A3 recorded a FALSE GREEN from exactly that. The driver
rebuilds `@platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy` before every run, and the two
mutations that touch `packages/contexts/**` are not in this ledger for that
reason: there are none. Every source mutation here is inside the adapter.

baseline.note: 19 container cases + 9 that read the schema, the migrations and the taxonomy off disk.

mutations.name: M01 RatingTargetReader loses the tenant join
mutations.guards: governance-seam-conversations.ts — `find`, the one place a turn's tenancy is decided
mutations.why: `Turn` has NO `environmentId` column: its tenancy is its thread's. `findFirst` with the relation filter removed still compiles, still answers a well-formed turn id, and answers ANY tenant's turn.
kills: × RatingTargetReader > a turn in ANOTHER tenant is null, not the row
× RatingTargetReader > a REAL environment under a FOREIGN project is null — the whole triple narrows
mutations.note: The second kill is the ORACLE's clause: `threadScopeWhere` narrows by project and organization too.

mutations.name: M02 TranscriptReader loses the tenant filter on the thread
mutations.guards: governance-seam-conversations.ts — `read`, before any turn is loaded
mutations.why: This is the read a judge is PAID to consume. Losing the filter hands a model another tenant's whole conversation and bills for it.
kills: × TranscriptReader > a thread in ANOTHER tenant is null, and its own scope can still read it
× TranscriptReader > a REAL environment under a FOREIGN project is null — the whole triple narrows

mutations.name: M03 a named turn stops narrowing the transcript
mutations.guards: governance-seam-conversations.ts — the `id` filter on the turn read
mutations.why: The port says a named turn that is not in the thread yields an EMPTY list rather than the whole thread, so 'a mistyped id cannot silently widen what a judge is paid to read'.
kills: × TranscriptReader > a named turn narrows to one exchange
× TranscriptReader > a named turn from ANOTHER THREAD yields an empty list, not the whole thread
mutations.note: The second case uses a REAL id — the foreign tenant's turn — so a reader that dropped the filter on a miss answers with this thread's turns and is paid to score them.

mutations.name: M04 the transcript stops excluding CANCELLED turns
mutations.why: `read-seams.ts`: 'In conversation order. A cancelled turn is not included.' An abandoned exchange scored by a judge is evidence about nothing.
kills: × TranscriptReader > reads the thread in conversation order, without the cancelled turn
mutations.note: Only kills because the suite SEEDS a cancelled turn; without the seed the port's rule would be a claim about an empty set.

mutations.name: M05 the transcript loses conversation order
mutations.why: A judge shown a reversed conversation scores the assistant answering before it was asked.
kills: × TranscriptReader > reads the thread in conversation order, without the cancelled turn

mutations.name: M06 a mistyped turn id becomes a refusal instead of absence
mutations.why: The port's concealment: a turn in another environment and a typo must answer identically. A refusal on the malformed shape is a channel that tells the two apart.
mutations.to: if (rowId === null) return err(ratingTargetUnreadable("malformed turn id"));
kills: × RatingTargetReader > a mistyped turn id is ABSENT, not an error

mutations.name: M07 two of the three seams share one refusal code
mutations.why: Two guards sharing a code cannot be told apart. These three are ONE guard over ONE value in three files, which is the exact shape that collapses by accident.
mutations.from: return err(transcriptUnreadable(`no tenant to narrow by: ${resolvePath(scope)}`));
mutations.to: return err(ratingTargetUnreadable(`no tenant to narrow by: ${resolvePath(scope)}`));
kills: × TranscriptReader > a scope with no environment to narrow by REFUSES, under its own code
× the three seams refuse under three DISTINCT codes
mutations.note: The second kill is over the LIVE objects rather than the catalogue, so a seam wired to the wrong constructor fails there even if the catalogue is intact.

mutations.name: M08 the guard stops checking the PROJECT is a uuid
mutations.why: A non-uuid project reaches a `@db.Uuid` column, the driver raises, `refuse()` folds it into GOVERNANCE_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE — the shared code the three constructors exist to stay out of.
kills: × every LIMB of the tenant triple refuses, not only the environment
mutations.note: SURVIVED ON THE FIRST RUN (27 passed, exit 0). The suite blanked the ENVIRONMENT and never the other two limbs. A nineteenth case was added and this now kills.

mutations.name: M09 the guard stops checking the ENVIRONMENT is a uuid
mutations.why: Same as M08 for the limb the suite did cover from the start.
kills: × RatingTargetReader > a scope with no environment to narrow by REFUSES, under its own code
× TranscriptReader > a scope with no environment to narrow by REFUSES, under its own code
× ActivityReader > a scope with no environment to narrow by REFUSES rather than answering []
× the three seams refuse under three DISTINCT codes

mutations.guards: governance-seam-activity.ts — the two extra JOINs on the raw statement
mutations.why: The raw statement reaches the project through two JOINs the two grouped reads reach in one relation hop, so it is the one most easily left behind when the triple is added.

AND ${projectId}::uuid IS NOT NULL

kills: × ActivityReader > a REAL environment under a FOREIGN project counts NOTHING
mutations.note: The parameters stay bound so the mutation is a NARROWING change and not an unused-variable change.

mutations.name: M11 the turn count stops narrowing by environment
mutations.why: `risk.ts` divides by `Math.max(1, turns)`, so an inflated denominator quietly DEFLATES every rate on the board and an agent over the threshold drops below it. No error, no empty page, nothing to notice.
kills: × ActivityReader > a REAL environment under a FOREIGN project counts NOTHING
mutations.note: ONE kill and not three, and that is honest rather than weak: the project and organization clauses still narrow, so the plain cross-tenant cases stay green. Only the tampered triple — every identifier real, the relation between them a lie — separates them.

mutations.name: M12 the tool-error count stops narrowing by tenant
mutations.why: One of three differently-shaped narrowings in one method; the whole point of asserting the three counts separately is that a narrowing lost on ONE of them is invisible in a total.

× ActivityReader > each of the three counts is narrowed SEPARATELY
× ActivityReader > a REAL environment under a FOREIGN project counts NOTHING

mutations.why: A window that does not close is a risk board measuring all of history against thirty days of numerators.

kills: × ActivityReader > `since` closes the window from below

mutations.name: M14 tool errors count FAILED alone, not FAILED or CANCELLED
mutations.why: THIS IS THE DEFECT THE ORACLE FOUND. `apps/agent/src/monitoring/governance.service.ts` counts `status === 'FAILED' || status === 'CANCELLED'`. FAILED alone lowers every agent's tool-error rate, and a smaller number on a risk board looks like good news.
kills: × ActivityReader > counts turns, tool failures and approvals for THIS environment's agents
× ActivityReader > each of the three counts is narrowed SEPARATELY
mutations.note: The mutation IS the code as first written on this branch. It is in the ledger because it shipped green through 27 cases before the oracle was read; the CANCELLED row is now seeded so it cannot again.

mutations.name: M15 the activity reader answers [] instead of refusing
mutations.why: The most dangerous of the three to get wrong. `risk-report.ts` does not refuse on an activity failure — it renders the board with every denominator substituted and `complete: false`. An empty list is indistinguishable from a quiet installation.

oracle.name: O01 the tenant narrowing was the ENVIRONMENT alone
oracle.oracle: apps/agent/src/evals/rating.service.ts:74 `threadScopeWhere`, and the four denominator reads in apps/agent/src/monitoring/governance.service.ts — both byte-identical to origin/main
oracle.oracle-shape: { environmentId, environment: { project: { id: projectId, organizationId } } }
oracle.why-it-matters: `Environment.id` is a globally unique uuid, so the extra clauses look redundant. The scope they refuse is a REAL environment carrying SOMEBODY ELSE'S project or organization — a grant that has been tampered with, or built by a bug in whatever resolved it. All three readers served it.
oracle.why-no-mutation-found-it: Every assertion on this branch compared the readers to themselves. The scope cannot even be BUILT without two tenants on the table, and no case constructed one until the oracle said to.
oracle.resolution: All three readers narrow by the whole triple. Three integration cases build exactly that scope. The FIVE canonical governance stores beside them still use `governance-rows.ts`' `scopedWhere`, which is `{ environmentId }` alone — REPORTED, not repaired: widening it is a change to five ports this tranche does not own.

oracle.name: O02 `toolErrors` counted FAILED alone
oracle.why-it-matters: A narrower predicate LOWERS every agent's tool-error rate, and a smaller number on a risk board looks like good news rather than like a regression.
oracle.resolution: `status: { in: ["FAILED", "CANCELLED"] }`, a CANCELLED row seeded, and M14 in this ledger is the first draft as a mutation.

oracle.name: O03 a divergence KEPT, because the port asks for it
oracle.why-diverged: `read-seams.ts` names this a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE in writing: stamping a rating with whichever version is live now credits a promotion with the old version's output, which silently corrupts `readVersionSatisfaction` — the rollup a canary decision is taken on. Recorded here so the divergence is not mistaken for O01's kind.

declared.name: D01 THE CASCADE ON `AgentEval.criterion` — an OPEN FOUNDER DECISION, not touched
declared.claim: `AgentEval.criterion` is `onDelete: Cascade`, which defeats `criterionSnapshot`: the snapshot exists so a deleted criterion's evals stay interpretable, and the cascade destroys the evals instead.
declared.why-not-mutated: It is an open founder decision and this tranche was told not to fix it. What is recorded instead is WHERE IT BITES for these three readers, which is the question the brief asked.
declared.where-it-bites: NOWHERE IN THESE THREE. Measured rather than assumed: none of the three seams reads `AgentEval` or `EvalCriterion`. They read `Thread`, `Turn`, `ToolCallAudit` and `AgentApproval`. The nearest approach is `TranscriptReader`, which resolves the thread an eval was taken over — but a cascade that removes the EVAL leaves the thread and its turns untouched, so a transcript re-read after a criterion deletion is byte-identical. The cascade destroys the interpretation, not the evidence.
declared.adjacent-cascade-that-does-touch-them: `AgentApproval.turn` and `AgentApproval.thread` are BOTH `onDelete: Cascade` (initial migration). Deleting a turn therefore deletes its approvals, so `ActivityReader.approvalEvents` falls for a window whose turns have been erased while `SafetyLedger`'s numerators — `SafetyEvent.turnId` is also Cascade — fall with them. The two move together, which is why no risk rate is distorted by it. Recorded, not changed.

declared.name: D02 CONCURRENT READERS INSIDE ONE UNIT OF WORK — declared unfalsifiable here, with the reason
declared.claim: `rate-turn.ts` reads the turn back inside the transaction that writes the rating, so `createGovernanceReadSeams` takes the same `TenancyTransactions` and resolves through `transactions.reader()`, which inside a unit of work IS the caller's client.
declared.why-not-mutated: The mutation — building the seams over `transactions.pool()` instead — is REJECTED BY THE TYPE SYSTEM at no point and would be killed only by a case that writes a rating and reads its turn back in one transaction. That case belongs to `rate-turn.ts`'s own suite in `packages/contexts/governance`, which runs against in-memory doubles and has no transaction to lose; the adapter-side suite that could hold it would be a `RatingsRepository` + read-seam integration case, which is a use-case-level test this tranche did not add.
declared.measured-instead: `createGovernanceReadSeams(transactions)` takes the same object `createGovernanceStores(transactions)` does, from the same call site in `adapter.ts`, and `transaction.ts`' `reader()` is `ambient.getStore()?.client ?? client`. The property is structural and stated; it is NOT proven by a red test on this branch, and that is said here rather than implied.
